name: Orthodox Trotskyism
summary: Orthodox Trotskyism is the current of the Fourth International that claims fidelity to Trotsky's 1938 Transitional Programme and to his view of the USSR as a degenerated workers' state. It calls for independent revolutionary parties, soviets and workers' control leading to a workers' state, rejects Stalinism, popular fronts and socialism in one country, and opposes the 'Pabloist' revisionism it split from in 1953.
scope: The groups that claim fidelity to the 1938 Transitional Programme against revisionists: the International Committee of the Fourth International (its Socialist Equality Parties), the Spartacist tendency (ICL) and Cannon's SWP at the 1953 Open Letter, plus Trotsky's texts as they adopted them (Revolution Betrayed, Their Morals and Ours). Trotskyism as a whole, state-capitalist Trotskyists (Cliff) and Pabloites are excluded. Where only one group states a position and the others are silent, the answer is null; the documents read are programmes, not the groups' every pamphlet.

public-ownership.rationale: The Transitional Programme demands expropriating the banks and key trusts and the programmes aim at collectivised, planned property.

property-fundamental.rationale: The programme's aim is the expropriation of the bourgeoisie, so private property is not a right to be protected.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Orthodox programmes set a democratically planned economy against capitalist market anarchy and call capitalism beyond reform.

central-planning.rationale: The Open Letter and the Spartacist declaration both call for a planned, collectivised economy as the answer to capitalist crisis.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Transitional Programme makes workers' control of industry, opening the books of capital, a core demand and a school for planning.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Transitional Programme treats the right to employment, shared work through a sliding scale of hours and public works, as the one serious right left to workers.

cut-welfare.rationale: The programme has the party defend the social conquests of the workers and oppose austerity; it holds no view that welfare breeds dependency.

unions-good.rationale: The programme tells revolutionaries to work in the mass unions and strengthen them, while fighting their bureaucratic leaders.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme merges the banks into one state credit institution to direct investment under a plan.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The programme puts the whole credit system in the hands of the state under workers' control, which excludes an independent bank.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Trotsky treats 'to each according to needs' as the principle of the higher stage of communism that the Soviet bureaucracy only pretended to apply.

production-for-use.rationale: The ICFI programme makes planning for social needs rather than profit the purpose of a socialised economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The ICFI programme names capitalism as the main source of exploitation; the Marxist theory of surplus value is Trotsky's own.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed analyses prices, profit and the Soviet economy using Marx's law of value and surplus value.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Trotsky holds that in the transition income follows labour done, not property owned; ownership income is abolished with the bourgeoisie.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The ICFI programme argues there can be no democracy without socialism because economic inequality destroys political equality.

corporate-influence.rationale: Both the programme and the ICFI statement describe the banks and trusts as commanding the state and the media.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The ICFI statements condemn corporate domination of the media and state censorship as undermining democracy.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The ICFI statements, Spartacist declaration and Transitional Programme all state that imperialist rivalry inevitably produces war.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Open Letter and the Transitional Programme describe capitalism as in its death agony, answerable only by socialist revolution.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Transitional Programme says capitalism has already built the economic prerequisites for socialism, now stagnating under private ownership.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Trotsky's programme builds socialism on the productive forces capitalism created and blames only their private ownership.

free-trade.rationale: The ICFI statement rejects both free trade and protectionism as capitalist policies.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The ICFI statements reject protectionism together with free trade, as nationalist and capitalist.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Trotsky's programme treats stagnating productive forces as the objective basis of revolution, and the ICFI statement affirms materialism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Their Morals and Ours calls the class struggle the driving force of the evolution of social forms.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The ICFI statement calls the bourgeois state an instrument of capitalist class dictatorship, and the Spartacist declaration agrees.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Spartacist declaration calls for the dictatorship of the proletariat on councils, and the ICFI statement for a workers' state.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Spartacist declaration says the capitalist state must be smashed, and the ICFI statements call for abolishing its standing army and security apparatus.

workers-councils.rationale: The Transitional Programme makes soviets the organ of power, and the Spartacist declaration a workers' government based on councils.

vanguard-party.rationale: The ICFI statement, the Spartacist declaration and Cannon all hold that socialist consciousness has to be brought into the class by a Marxist party.

revolution-justified.rationale: Socialist revolution led by the working class is the central aim of every orthodox programme.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The ICFI statement, the Spartacist declaration and the Transitional Programme reject socialism in one country and require world revolution.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Trotsky rejects the label state capitalism for the USSR, and orthodox groups (ICL) defend its degenerated workers' state character.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Trotsky and the Spartacist declaration call for unconditional defence of nationalised property against imperialism, while demanding political revolution against the bureaucracy.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed rejects Stalin's doctrine of a strengthening state: a workers' state should begin to wither, and its growth marks bureaucratic degeneration.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Trotsky calls the USSR not socialist because the workers hold no power and demands political revolution; the ICFI says no socialism without democracy.

independent-unions.rationale: The Spartacist declaration demands unions be unconditionally independent of the state and the Transitional Programme opposes state tutelage of unions.

workers-own-party.rationale: The ICFI statements demand a break with the Democrats and Labour, the Spartacists reject popular fronts, and the Open Letter urges a labor party.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Spartacist declaration opposes coalitions with capitalist parties in principle, and the Transitional Programme denounces the People's Front.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Spartacist declaration commits to revolutionary defeatism in inter-imperialist wars; the ICFI statements demand withdrawal and oppose imperialist war.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The ICFI statement, Spartacist declaration and the Open Letter all state democratic centralism: debate, then binding decisions.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Spartacist declaration defends proletarian rights to strike and picket, and demands cops and courts out of union affairs.

industrial-unions.rationale: The Spartacist declaration supports industrial unionism and opposes craft divisions among workers.

one-party-rule.rationale: Trotsky's mature position in The Revolution Betrayed demands a revival of freedom for Soviet parties, starting with the Bolshevik party.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed demands genuine freedom of elections, the right of criticism and independent unions in the USSR.

party-controls-media.rationale: Trotsky demands the right of criticism in the USSR and the ICFI condemns censorship; no orthodox text asks for party control of media.

recall-officials.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed approves the Bolshevik programme of election and recall at any time of all officials.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Bolshevik programme Trotsky defends makes plenipotentiaries subject to recall at any time and active control by the masses.

leader-cult.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed condemns the Stalinist cult of the leader and the privileges of the bureaucratic caste.

state-harmful.rationale: The Spartacist declaration rejects anarchism and calls for a workers' state that withers only with classless communism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programmes demand a planned, nationalised economy and a workers' state, not a minimal one.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programmes call for a workers' state and workers' militia in place of the capitalist state's armed forces.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Expropriating the bourgeoisie and smashing the state by revolution contradict a rule against ever initiating force.

political-violence-never.rationale: Orthodox programmes call for revolution and defend armed workers' defence guards, though the ICFI condemns individual terror.

universal-morality.rationale: Their Morals and Ours argues morality is a function of the class struggle and rejects eternal moral truths.

means-match-ends.rationale: Trotsky holds that the liberating end requires means that raise the masses' consciousness and rejects lies and individual terror, while denying means are independent of ends.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Spartacist declaration calls the police hired guns of the capitalist state; the ICFI wants the standing army and security apparatus abolished.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The ICFI statements condemn police-state measures and the erosion of civil liberties under the pretext of terrorism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Trotsky criticised the Soviet substitution of a standing army for the militia, and the ICFI wants the standing army abolished.

military-superiority.rationale: The programmes oppose imperialist armaments and war ('not a man and not a penny') and demand withdrawal of forces abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Open Letter condemns Soviet troops crushing the East German workers' uprising and demands their withdrawal.

nation-first.rationale: Orthodox programmes are internationalist and reject the substitution of nationalism for internationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether military intervention abroad is sometimes necessary to protect human rights, and this disagreement rested on opposing particular interventions or interventions by particular powers, which doesn't say it is never necessary.

reviewHistory.rationale: The ICFI statements condemn imperialist wars fought on human-rights pretexts and demand withdrawal from Iraq and Afghanistan.

open-borders.rationale: The ICFI statements assert the right of workers to live and work where they choose and the elimination of national borders.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The ICFI statements oppose border controls and anti-immigrant laws, and the Spartacists demand full citizenship rights for all immigrants.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The ICFI and Spartacist programmes demand full rights and citizenship for all immigrants.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The programmes demand full citizenship rights for all immigrants, including undocumented ones.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Spartacist declaration affirms self-determination for all nations, subordinated to class struggle, while the ICFI rejects separatist nationalisms such as the SNP.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Spartacists affirm the right of self-determination while the ICFI statement opposes separatist movements in practice, so the right is held but not championed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Transitional Programme and the Spartacist declaration hold that colonial democratic tasks can only be completed by the proletariat taking power and transforming property.

traditional-family.rationale: Trotsky calls the old family a stifling institution the revolution tried to abolish, and the Spartacists tie women's liberation to abolishing the family.

abortion-legal.rationale: Trotsky calls the right to abortion an important civil and cultural right, and the Spartacist declaration demands free legal abortion.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Trotsky and the Spartacist declaration say women's liberation requires socialist revolution and socialising housework.

socialized-care.rationale: Trotsky holds that housework and child care must be absorbed by social institutions for women's real liberation.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Spartacist declaration opposes laws criminalising consensual same-sex activity, and the ICFI demands an end to discrimination by sexuality.

women-suffrage.rationale: The ICFI statements demand full equality and abolition of gender discrimination, and the Spartacists equal rights for women.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The ICFI and Spartacist programmes demand the abolition of all discrimination by race, gender, religion or nationality.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The orthodox Trotskyist texts read record no shared position on this statement, and no stated principle settles it.
